claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a lamellar microstructure comprising ordered FCC L12 and ordered BCC B2 phases.
The L12 phase constitutes approximately 65 vol% of the initial alloy.
The B2 phase constitutes approximately 35 vol% of the initial alloy.
The as-cast alloy undergoes catastrophic interfacial cracking and has low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
HPT at 77 K and 6-8 GPa for 2-3 turns followed by annealing at 600-700°C for 1-2 hours will transform the lamellar alloy into patterned ultrafine-grained, deformation-twinned domains.
The transformed microstructure will contain coherent twin boundaries with spacing below 100 nm that replace continuous lamellar interfaces with a tortuous interconnected network.
Cryogenic processing stabilizes or retains the B2 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Cryogenic HPT will induce massive deformation twinning in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The extreme HPT pressure suppresses void nucleation.
The extreme pressure promotes homogeneous shear or controls shear localization.
Post-HPT annealing will stabilize the twin-boundary network and produce a partially recrystallized patterned configuration.
Coherent twin boundaries strengthen the material by interacting with and impeding dislocations.
The twin-boundary network will deflect and arrest propagating cracks.
Coherent twin boundaries will minimize interfacial stress concentration.
Twinning-induced plasticity will promote uniform plastic deformation in the treated alloy.
Transformation-induced plasticity will promote uniform plastic deformation in the treated alloy.
Ultrafine grains will enhance strength through Hall-Petch strengthening.
The treated alloy will exceed 20% tensile elongation at room temperature.
The treated alloy will retain or exceed a yield strength of 1 GPa.
A ductility difference between cryogenic HPT-treated and 1000°C/100 MPa HIP-treated samples would establish that extreme pressure and HPT shear are essential.

contradictions.description: The HIP comparison does not isolate extreme pressure because it simultaneously changes pressure, deformation mode, and temperature: HPT uses 6-8 GPa, torsional shear, and 77 K, whereas HIP uses 100 MPa, no severe shear, and 1000°C. Any property difference therefore cannot be attributed specifically to extreme pressure.
